tipo_en: High (~2,800 m), cold, dry basin with salts and yardangs

works: Ancient lake that dried out leaving salts and sulfates, as in Gale
Cold, dry, high and with strong UV
breaks: Air pressure ~70 kPa, far above Mars

tipo_en: Giant wind-carved yardangs and some of the highest surface temperatures MODIS has measured

works: Yardangs like those of Medusae Fossae on Mars
Almost lifeless, no vegetation
breaks: Extreme heat, the opposite of Mars

tipo_en: Hyperarid core, the driest non-polar place on Earth

works: Nearly sterile soil with perchlorates, like those Phoenix found on Mars
Dry, with very strong UV

tipo_en: Hyperacidic, salty hot springs below sea level

works: Acidic iron- and sulfate-rich brines, like ancient Meridiani
Shows the limit of life: some pools are sterile

tipo_en: Coastal dune field with seasonal lagoons

works: Active dunes with short-lived water between them, as proposed for early Mars
Loose sand to test wheels (Spirit got stuck in sand)

tipo_en: ~23 km impact crater in a polar desert

works: Crater in a polar desert with permafrost
Low sun and polar day

tipo_en: Semi-arid sandstone plateau with bare soil

works: Dust on solar panels, as on Mars rovers
Bare soil and strong sun
breaks: Still ~500 mm of rain a year (NASA POWER)
Caatinga scrub covers part of the ground

tipo_en: Gullies and bare soil: Brazil's largest desertification core

works: Bare reddish soil and ravines, like eroded Martian terrain
Fast erosion that satellites can measure
breaks: Erosion here is by running water, which on Mars existed only in the past

tipo_en: Volcanoes with carbonate globules in basalt, inside Arctic permafrost

works: Carbonates in basalt like those in Martian meteorite ALH84001 and at Jezero
Midnight sun and polar night: low light like the lunar south pole
breaks: Ice, snow and sea all around

tipo_en: Acidic river rich in iron and sulfates

works: Jarosite and hematite, the Meridiani minerals
Life in acidic water and underground (MARTE project)
breaks: Mining and a town around it

tipo_en: Basaltic volcano with cinder and ash cones

works: Pu'u Nene ash became the JSC Mars-1 Martian soil simulant
NASA ISRU (oxygen extraction) tests with volcanic regolith

tipo_en: Young (~1.8 km) crater in Deccan basalt with a salty alkaline lake

works: One of few well-preserved craters in basalt, like those on the Moon and Mars
Salt lake in the crater recalls the ancient lakes of Jezero and Gale
breaks: Monsoons and dense vegetation on the rim

tipo_en: ~13 km complex crater with a central ring, in sedimentary rock

works: Central ring and rim very well exposed, as in complex Martian craters
Dry-season cerrado leaves the rock exposed

tipo_en: South America's largest impact structure (~40 km), with an uplifted granite core

works: Large crater scale, comparable to Mars landing craters
Uplifted core brings deep rock to the surface, like lunar central peaks

tipo_en: ~12 km complex impact crater in basalt

works: Impact into basalt, the rock of the lunar maria and the Martian crust
Shock features and breccias in volcanic rock, rare worldwide
breaks: Humid climate and vegetation cover the rock
Strong erosion has erased part of the rim

works: A second basalt impact in the same province: two craters to compare
Accessible impact breccias in basalt
breaks: Town and farmland inside the crater

tipo_en: Canga (iron crust) plateaus with over 1,000 caves

works: Hematite and goethite, the oxides that color Mars and that Opportunity found at Meridiani
Caves to train underground exploration, like pits and lava tubes
breaks: Caves in iron rock, not lava tubes

tipo_en: Ice-free polar desert with permafrost and salt lakes

works: The coldest, driest place on Earth: buried ice like Arcadia
Polar night and low sun, like the lunar south pole
breaks: Still about −20 °C on average, far from −200 °C
